name: Convert between units of length
description: Student can convert between metric units of length.
exampleOfSuccess: The student converts 2.5 m to 250 cm.
commonError: Student multiplies when they should divide, or uses the wrong factor.
checkpointTask: Pose length conversions. Ask the student to convert each.

name: Convert between units of mass and capacity
description: Student can convert between metric units of mass and capacity.
exampleOfSuccess: The student converts 1500 g to 1.5 kg and 2000 mL to 2 L.
commonError: Student uses the wrong conversion factor, or the wrong operation.
checkpointTask: Pose mass and capacity conversions. Ask the student to convert each.

name: Use the prefixes in metric units
description: Student can use the meaning of metric prefixes to reason about conversions.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains that kilo means a thousand, so 1 km is 1000 m.
commonError: Student memorises conversions without understanding the prefixes.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to explain conversions using the meaning of the prefixes.

name: Choose a decimal representation for a context
description: Student can choose and use a decimal representation of a measurement for a context.
exampleOfSuccess: The student records 125 cm as 1.25 m where metres suit the problem.
commonError: Student keeps an awkward unit that does not suit the context.
checkpointTask: Pose measurement problems. Ask the student to choose a suitable decimal representation.

name: Establish the area formula for a rectangle
description: Student can establish that the area of a rectangle is length times width.
exampleOfSuccess: Using grid paper, the student sees a 4 by 3 rectangle has 12 squares, so area is 4 x 3.
commonError: Student counts only the border, or adds the side lengths.
checkpointTask: Use grid paper. Ask the student to find the rule connecting the sides to the area.

name: Use the formula to find area
description: Student can use the area formula to find the area of a rectangle.
exampleOfSuccess: For an 8 m by 5 m rectangle, the student finds 40 square metres.
commonError: Student adds the sides instead of multiplying.
checkpointTask: Give rectangles with labelled sides. Ask the student to find the area.

name: Solve a practical area problem
description: Student can use the area formula to solve a practical problem.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds how many tiles cover a floor using its area.
commonError: Student finds perimeter, or uses mismatched units.
checkpointTask: Pose practical area problems. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Compare lengths and areas
description: Student can compare how changing the sides affects the area.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notices doubling both sides makes the area four times as large.
commonError: Student assumes doubling the sides doubles the area.
checkpointTask: Pose rectangles with changed sides. Ask the student to compare the areas.

name: Read a timetable
description: Student can read a timetable to find departure and arrival times.
exampleOfSuccess: From a bus timetable, the student finds when the next bus leaves.
commonError: Student reads across the wrong row or column.
checkpointTask: Give a timetable. Ask the student to find given times.

name: Find the duration of a journey
description: Student can use a timetable to find the duration of a journey.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds a trip from 9:15 to 10:05 takes 50 minutes.
commonError: Student subtracts the digits without regard to 60 minutes in an hour.
checkpointTask: Give a timetable. Ask the student to find journey durations.

name: Plan a journey using timetables
description: Student can plan a journey involving one or more modes of transport using timetables.
exampleOfSuccess: The student plans a trip with a bus then a train, allowing for the connection.
commonError: Student plans a connection that does not allow enough time.
checkpointTask: Give timetables. Ask the student to plan a journey with a connection.

name: Plan an itinerary
description: Student can create an itinerary of activities with durations.
exampleOfSuccess: The student builds a day plan with start times and durations that fit.
commonError: Student plans activities that overlap or leave gaps unaccounted for.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to plan an itinerary of activities with times and durations.

name: Use angles on a straight line
description: Student can use the fact that angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees.
exampleOfSuccess: Given one angle of 110 degrees on a line, the student finds the other is 70.
commonError: Student assumes the angles are equal, or uses 360 instead of 180.
checkpointTask: Pose angles on a straight line with one unknown. Ask the student to find it.

name: Use angles at a point
description: Student can use the fact that angles at a point sum to 360 degrees.
exampleOfSuccess: Given three angles at a point, the student finds the fourth.
commonError: Student uses 180 instead of 360 for angles at a point.
checkpointTask: Pose angles at a point with one unknown. Ask the student to find it.

name: Use vertically opposite angles
description: Student can use the fact that vertically opposite angles are equal.
exampleOfSuccess: Where two lines cross, the student says the opposite angle is equal.
commonError: Student treats adjacent angles as equal instead of opposite ones.
checkpointTask: Show crossing lines. Ask the student to find the vertically opposite angle.

name: Find an unknown angle with reasoning
description: Student can determine an unknown angle and communicate the reasoning.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds an unknown angle and explains which rule they used.
commonError: Student finds the angle but cannot explain the reasoning.
checkpointTask: Pose angle problems. Ask the student to find the unknown and explain the reasoning.
